name: Seabed mud power cell
effect: seabed bacteria living on chemicals hand electrons to an electrode
how: A power source for ocean sensors that sits in the seabed mud for years. Bacteria in the mud live off its chemicals and dump spare electrons onto a buried electrode, which flow through a wire to a second electrode in the water above, giving a small but endless current.
why: Deep-sea chemical life as a battery that never needs replacing.
